sources.title: aas-test-engines (Official test tooling for the Asset Administration Shell)
sources.issuing_body: admin-shell-io GitHub organization. PyPI lists maintainer accounts bjoern.otto, juileetikekar, otto-ifak; the latest commits are by Bjoern Otto and juileetikekar. Any formal IDTA operating relationship was not verified in this audit.
sources.legal_or_spec_status: Released software, latest PyPI release 1.0.3. No commits and no releases since 2025-08-05 (about 14 months before 2026-10-13). Repository not archived; 17 open issues per GitHub API (README page showed 16 issues plus 1 pull request). No maintenance statement found. Not the same as unmaintained.
sources.license_or_reuse_terms: Apache-2.0 per GitHub licence detection (REST API spdx_id Apache-2.0). PyPI metadata has no license string (license field null) but lists a LICENSE file.
sources.permitted_use_basis: Apache-2.0 dependency or test tool; run locally against own AAS files or own servers only. Its homepage field points to a hosted validation service (validation-service.admin-shell-io.com), which this audit did not contact.

evidence.what_it_shows: Version 1.0.3 released 2025-08-05; release history; three maintainers; Requires-Python >=3.6; generic Python 3 classifier only; default checks are metamodel 3.0.1 and API 3.0.3 (version 3.0); submodel templates Contact Information (ZVEI nameplate 1/0) and Digital Nameplate for Industrial Equipment (nameplate 2/0); API profiles AAS, Submodel, Repository, Registry (read), Discovery Service, Concept Description Repository, some marked IDTA members only.

info.requires_python >=3.6; classifiers only Python and Python :: 3; license null; project_urls Homepage is the GitHub repository; upload_time 2025-08-05T08:51:53 for 1.0.3; full release list with times.
Repository page: Apache-2.0, 237 commits, 30 stars, not archived, CI badge; README default compliance target AAS version 3.0.

License Apache-2.0; pushed_at 2025-08-05T08:51:00Z; updated_at 2026-10-04T10:34:48Z (metadata or issue activity, not a code push); archived false; open_issues_count 17; created 2022-10-13; description 'Official test tooling for the Asset Administration Shell'.
Most recent commit 56facc4b 'Prepare v1.0.3' dated 2025-08-05T08:45:57Z; previous commits 2025-06-23 and 2025-06-22.
Empty list: no GitHub releases or tags.
Package aas_test_engines version 1.0.3; requires-python >=3.6; classifiers generic; dependencies dynamic from requirements.txt.
CI runs on push, one job on ubuntu-latest, Python set to '3.x' (single latest 3.x, no version matrix).

sources.brief_claim_check: matches: the tool exists under this name at the expected admin-shell-io location; the brief gave no specific values, so the located values are recorded here (Python support, spec versions and maintenance are three separate facts: requires_python >=3.6, CI on latest 3.x only, no per-version classifier).
uncertainties: Which AAS spec versions older than 3.0 are selectable was seen only in a search-result summary of the README, not confirmed on the page.
Python 3.12 support is neither declared by classifier nor tested by a matrix; CI uses whatever 3.x is latest at run time.
GitHub API updated_at (2026-10-04) differs from pushed_at (2025-08-05); treated as non-code activity.
Whether admin-shell-io is operated by IDTA was not verified.
The IDTA-members-only marking of some API profiles comes from the PyPI/README text and its conditions were not examined.

sources.title: java-dpp-sdk (Cir4Fun Java SDK for DPP system components)
sources.edition_or_version: Artifact version 0.5.1 stated in the repository documentation; no GitHub release or tag (REST releases list empty). Latest commit on main 31db77f4 dated 2026-08-10T14:47:09Z; GitHub API pushed_at 2026-09-29T17:39:08Z (not reconciled, possibly another branch). Created 2026-05-27.
sources.legal_or_spec_status: Public repository, pre-1.0 (0.5.1), unreleased on GitHub. README says no formal compliance, certification, legal-conformity or production-readiness claim is made.
sources.permitted_use_basis: Apache-2.0 dependency candidate for client-side use only. Not usable as a conformance oracle: its README states that some API contracts were designed with reference to confidential external specifications not included in the repository, and that it is not a formal compliance implementation.

evidence.what_it_shows: Java/Maven monorepo with modules dpp-datamodel, dpp-postgres, dpp-sdk-clients, dpp-sdk-demo; README states selected repository and registry API shapes implemented in alignment with EN 18222:2026 (a claim by the README, not verified here); partial RFC 7396 and RFC 9535 support; listed misalignments (no backup-operator field or operation, project-defined compressed representation, application/json instead of merge-patch for partial updates); no compliance claim; confidential external specifications referenced; local Docker demo only, no hosted instance, no credentials or terms listed.
Empty list: no releases.
Latest main commits 2026-08-10T14:47:09Z (merge of feat/java-sdk-contract-evidence) and 2026-08-06T12:12:52Z.
License Apache-2.0; pushed_at 2026-09-29T17:39:08Z; created 2026-05-27T09:33:40Z; language Java; not archived.

sources.brief_claim_check: differs: the brief expected a CIR4FUN-EU SDK; the real Java SDK repository is named java-dpp-sdk and the Python one python-dpp-sdk (PyPI dpp-sdk).
uncertainties: Version 0.5.1 appears only in README text; no tag or release exists to confirm a publication date.
pushed_at (2026-09-29) is later than the latest main commit seen (2026-08-10); not reconciled.
README content was read via a page summarizer; repository-page 'Releases empty' statements are consistent with the REST API for this repo but proved unreliable for CIRPASS-2 repos (see anomalies).
The EN 18222:2026 alignment claim is the repository's own statement and is not confirmed here.

dpp-sdk 0.4.0 uploaded 2026-08-11T13:51:50; author Enno Mueller; summary 'Python SDK for interacting with Digital Product Passport (DPP) System Infrastructure'; project_urls point to gitlab.cc-asp.fraunhofer.de.
Release history 0.1.0, 0.1.1, 0.2.1, 0.4.0; Trusted Publishing provenance from github.com/CIR4FUN-EU/python-dpp-sdk; one maintainer account OnneM156.
Four undated entries; 0.4.0 'Synchronisation with java-dpp-sdk'.

sources.brief_claim_check: differs: the Python SDK repository is python-dpp-sdk but its PyPI name is dpp-sdk (pypi.org/pypi/python-dpp-sdk/json returned 404), and PyPI metadata links point to a Fraunhofer GitLab rather than the CIR4FUN-EU GitHub repository.
uncertainties: Relationship between the PyPI project_urls (Fraunhofer GitLab) and the GitHub CIR4FUN-EU publisher is unexplained; possible partner mirror or stale metadata. Verify before pinning the dependency.

sources.title: CIRPASS-2 Open Source Test Environment (description report, Zenodo)
sources.issuing_body: CIRPASS-2 consortium (EU Digital Europe Programme, GA No 101158775). Zenodo record creator: Marco Volpini (ExtraRed). The website footer names F6S Network Ireland Limited as Website Manager for cirpass2.eu.
sources.edition_or_version: Zenodo v1; publication date 2026-06-16; record created and modified 2026-06-18; single file CIRPASS2_TestEnvironment_Description.pdf (378.5 kB). The cirpass2.eu project-results page dates the item 2026-06-16.
sources.legal_or_spec_status: Project result (report). The environment it describes is a set of open-source, configurable tools: a Mock EU Registry and an EU Web Portal (DPP Renderer), complemented by a DPP Validation Service and a DPP Data Extractor. Per the repository READMEs these are example and experimental, not normative, and are self-deployed; no hosted public instance is documented in any official source examined.
sources.license_or_reuse_terms: The report is CC BY 4.0. The tools are Apache-2.0 (see cirpass2-github-repositories). The cirpass2.eu Terms of Use cover only the website and Materials made available through it, not the self-deployed tools.
sources.permitted_use_basis: Metadata and documentation reference only. Do not treat the environment as a normative oracle: the READMEs state the artifacts are for exploration and information, not complete or normative. This audit did not access any CIRPASS-2 environment.

evidence.what_it_shows: Lists 'CIRPASS-2 Open Source Test Environment' dated 2026-06-16 with the component description; names no operator; links only to the Zenodo record; states no access conditions or terms.
Title, creator Marco Volpini (ExtraRed), 2026-06-16, v1, report, CC BY 4.0, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20749604, single PDF; no abstract; no repository or hosted-environment link; Zenodo terms apply.
Fetch attempted; the PDF text layer could not be parsed by WebFetch (13 pages, A4, en-GB visible in raw structure only). Content NOT read.

Terms of Use scope is the Website and Materials made available via it; Website Manager is F6S Network Ireland Limited; Irish law; prohibits scraping and automated access without consent; no mention of a test environment.

Project funded under GA No 101158775; 36 months; links to GitHub organization https://github.com/CIRPASS-2 as the repositories of open-source code; no test environment, hosted instance or access terms stated.
OpenDPP Catalogue directory of third-party open-source tools hosted on the project site; no statement about the test environment.

sources.brief_claim_check: differs: the brief presumes an environment with access conditions; every official source examined describes a self-deployed local Docker Compose stack of example tools, with no hosted public instance documented, and the description PDF itself could not be read.
uncertainties: The description PDF (the primary public documentation) was not parsed, so statements about a hosted instance, access conditions or terms in that PDF are unknown.

A trade-press item (ecotextile.com, returned 403) says textile suppliers can apply to a Plasafe-led pilot 'on the CIRPASS-2 platform'; a hosted pilot platform and its terms were not located in official sources and are discovery evidence only.
Project duration is stated inconsistently in secondary sources (May 2024 to April 2027 versus July 2024 to September 2026); the official site says 36 months only.

sources.title: CIRPASS-2 GitHub repositories (mock-eu-registry, dpp-validator, dpp-data-extractor, dpp-renderer-be, dpp-renderer-fe, deploy-resources, ontologies)
sources.issuing_body: CIRPASS-2 Consortium (copyright notice 2024-2027; funded by the EU Digital Europe Programme, GA No 101158775)
sources.edition_or_version: 13 public repositories, none archived. Per repo (GitHub REST releases and pushed_at): mock-eu-registry latest release 1.1.1-pgsql-oidc and 1.1.1-mariadb-oidc on 2026-07-01 (16 releases in total, 1.0.1 from 2025-12-02), pushed 2026-08-04; dpp-validator latest release seen 1.0.2-pgsql-oidc on 2026-04-17, pushed 2026-08-04; dpp-data-extractor latest release seen 1.0.2-pgsql-oidc and mariadb-oidc on 2026-06-11, pushed 2026-08-04; dpp-renderer-be latest release seen 1.0.2-pgsql-oidc and mariadb-oidc on 2026-06-11, pushed 2026-06-11; dpp-renderer-fe latest release 1.1.0 on 2026-09-23 (1.0.1 on 2026-04-20, 1.0.0 on 2026-03-20), pushed 2026-09-23; deploy-resources pushed 2026-06-10; ontologies-tyre pushed 2026-10-13; ontologies-battery 2026-10-06; documentation-battery 2026-10-06; ontologies-docs 2026-10-12; ontologie-textiles (no licence) 2026-09-28; actions 2026-03-20; assets 2026-06-11.
sources.legal_or_spec_status: Active public repositories. READMEs describe mock-eu-registry as an 'example and experimental application' based on the authors' assumptions, noting that EU-level standardization of DPP registries is still ongoing; all READMEs carry a disclaimer that artifacts are for exploration and information, not complete, exhaustive or normative, and that interpretations are the authors' own and not those of the EU, the Commission, HADEA or CEN-CENELEC JTC 24.
sources.license_or_reuse_terms: Apache-2.0 for the software repositories listed (mock-eu-registry, dpp-validator, dpp-data-extractor, dpp-renderer-be, dpp-renderer-fe, deploy-resources, actions, ontologies-*, documentation-battery, ontologies-docs); ontologie-textiles and assets show no licence.
sources.permitted_use_basis: Apache-2.0 dependency or local test harness, self-deployed. deploy-resources documents default credentials for a local Keycloak, databases and apps (credential values deliberately not repeated here). OIDC roles admin, eo (economic operator) and eu (end user) gate the APIs. Not a normative oracle.

evidence.what_it_shows: 13 repositories with licences, pushed_at, language, archived=false; documentation-battery homepage https://cirpass-2.github.io/documentation-battery/.

Docker Compose configurations for a local CIRPASS 2 test environment: Keycloak, two PostgreSQL databases, mock-eu-registry, dpp-validator, dpp-data-extractor, renderer-be, renderer-fe, all on localhost; no hosted URLs; disclaimer; Apache-2.0.

HTTP registry service for DPP metadata (PostgreSQL or MariaDB), OpenID Connect with roles admin/eo/eu, JSON Schema draft 2020-12 metadata validation, RS256-signed JWT proof of registration, detached JWS verification; 'example and experimental'; no hosted instance; Apache-2.0.
Validates JSON or JSON-LD DPP payloads against JSON Schema or SHACL templates; OIDC bearer tokens; starts with no schemas; no hosted instance listed; disclaimer; Apache-2.0.
Angular frontend to view, search and compare DPP data, QR-code scanning, management of validation resources for ADMIN/EU roles; no hosted instance URL; disclaimer; Apache-2.0.
16 non-prerelease releases from 1.0.1 (2025-12-02) to 1.1.1 (2026-07-01), pgsql-oidc and mariadb-oidc variants.
Latest releases 1.0.2-pgsql-oidc (2026-04-17) and 1.0.1-pgsql-oidc (2026-03-12).
Latest releases 1.0.2-pgsql-oidc and 1.0.2-mariadb-oidc (2026-06-11), 1.0.1-pgsql-oidc (2026-04-17).
Latest releases 1.0.2-pgsql-oidc and 1.0.2-mariadb-oidc (2026-06-11), 1.0.1-pgsql-oidc (2026-04-17).

sources.brief_claim_check: differs: the brief refers to a CIRPASS-2 test environment with access conditions; the repositories show self-deployed example tools under Apache-2.0 with a non-normative disclaimer, and no hosted instance.
uncertainties: Release lists were read from the REST API with per_page=3 for four repositories, so the latest three are shown, not full histories.
The 13th repository count includes actions and assets; contents of ontology repositories were not examined.
The HTML repository pages reported empty Releases sections where the REST API showed releases, so only API values are used for release data.

sources.title: zxing-cpp (Python bindings of the ZXing-C++ barcode library)

evidence.what_it_shows: requires_python >=3.9; license_expression Apache-2.0; classifiers only 'Python :: 3' (no 3.12 classifier); 31 files for 3.1.1 including zxing_cpp-3.1.1-cp312-abi3-macosx_11_0_arm64.whl and zxing_cpp-3.1.1-cp312-abi3-manylinux_2_27_x86_64.manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl (both uploaded 2026-07-29), also cp312-abi3 macosx_10_13_x86_64, manylinux aarch64, win_amd64, win_arm64, and cp310, cp311, cp313t and cp314t wheels plus sdist.
info.version 3.1.1; license_expression Apache-2.0; requires_python >=3.9 (the full document was too large to read in one pass).

sources.brief_claim_check: matches: binary wheels usable with CPython 3.12 exist for macOS arm64 and manylinux x86_64, but as abi3 wheels tagged cp312-abi3 rather than cp312-cp312, and the package declares no 3.12 classifier (only requires_python >=3.9).
uncertainties: Three separate facts: classifier (none for 3.12), requires_python (>=3.9), wheel tags (cp312-abi3 exist for the two targets).
The macOS arm64 wheel is tagged macosx_11_0_arm64 (not universal2); the Linux wheel carries manylinux_2_27/2_28 tags, which imply a glibc floor (inference from tag names, not tested).
The 3.13 and 3.14 wheels listed are free-threaded (cp313t, cp314t) builds; ordinary 3.13 and 3.14 are presumably covered by the cp312-abi3 wheels (inference).
Wheel list read through a page summarizer of the PyPI JSON.
